title: Where do people find playtesters for their games?
author: olafthemanofsnow
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I have been working on a story driven roulette roguelike and am looking for people to tear apart my game and provide me with some feedback. 

So far, over the last few months, a few of my friends have playtested a couple of iterations of it, and I have played it way too much as I have developed the game. 

But now I want to be brave/stupid as to put it out there with people who don't know me and have no reason to be kind, or to massage my ego. 

As a return, I will be more than happy to provide feedback and test your games.

If you are interested, please do reach out.

comments.author: forgingtheflow
comments.body: Search for the playtest subredits. Average fee is $10 per hour. Some people advertise doing it for free. Just be clear about what feedback you want.

comments.author: _-kman-_
comments.body:
I was going to propose the same thing for mine. 

Dm me. I'll trade you some time. :)

comments.author: Carter5on
comments.body: Usually, you announce it on your social media accounts, with a form of interest (name, email, etc.) and then you provide people that have filled in the form with access to a playtest build. Another option is to have a Demo published and ask for people to test it.

comments.author: boynet2
comments.body: you spend months on it, just run a ad in Facebook, get few players after you make sure you have analytics service and good events to understand what happening, its the best feedback ever, with the right ad you will get plenty, and just stop after like 20

comments.author: Valentinevandal1986
comments.body: What even is a “story driven roulette roguelike”?

replies.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
replies.body: It sounds like instead of a "choose your own adventure" story, you spin a wheel to see what happens next. I could be wrong though

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: So just a normal procedural/random story lmao

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body: If you were to give it enough “random choice” to make it interesting but keep it coherent, procedural can be fine. I’m working on a procedurally generated voxel adventure RPG that has castles and airships and boats, procedurally generated missions, it simulates the kingdom behind the scenes but I chose all the options in the system

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: I'm not saying otherwise, sounds cool, I was saying that the guy is using the usual throwing random words around to describe a pretty straightforward and common thing haha, which usually indicates they don't know what they're doing.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
If you have a WebGl build you can literally put it on platforms like Poki, Newgrounds, Kongregate.

Otherwise put it on Steam.

That said if I hear "roguelike" or "auto/idle/incremental" one more time I'll scream.
